body:
## Problem — head-of-line blocking

`commands.ts` returns from the queue loop on any non-`merged` terminal state:

```ts
const status = state?.pipelineState.status;
if (status !== "merged" && gi + 1 < groupList.length) {
  ... "queue halted. Remaining groups (…) were NOT started." ...
  return;
}
```

One issue's failure stops every unrelated issue behind it. This is textbook head-of-line blocking, and it is the single largest source of operator interruption in the harness.

## Evidence

From the forensic census of 22 cycles on this machine:

- `/work` with 13 issues: **#279 died and 11 unrelated groups never started.**
- `/work` with 5 issues: #277 died, 4 never started.
- `/work` with 2 issues: #308 died, 1 never started.
- A three-issue batch halted on its *second* item — #292 hit a review cap, and #323 never started despite being unrelated and independently ready.

**69% of the failures that trigger this are provider infrastructure**, not code quality (see #366) — so the queue is usually being stopped by something that has nothing to do with the remaining issues.

Worse, the operator is not reliably told: the `"queue halted … were NOT started"` string appears in **zero** of the 21 recorded session transcripts, despite at least four queue halts.

The documented rationale (`docs/troubleshooting.md:717`) is *"an intermediate handoff usually signals something the operator wants to review before we auto-start the next group."* In practice the halt **hides** that signal — it buries one reviewable handoff under N unstarted issues the operator must now re-drive by hand.

## What to build — three destinations, not two

Borrowing dead-letter-queue semantics, which solved exactly this decades ago in message processing:

- **`merged`** — continue.
- **`parked`** — issue-scoped failure. Record a structured entry (issue, reason, failing stage, attempt count, worktree path, and the human action required), then **continue with the next group**.
- **`halted`** — systemic failure only. The queue stops because continuing cannot work: `rate-limited:quota-terminal` (spend cap), `rate-limited:quota-window` (nothing will succeed until the reset), auth failure, or the driver throwing.

The distinction is the whole design: *is the next issue likely to fail for the same reason?* If yes, halt. If no, park and carry on.

## Also

- **End-of-queue report** naming what merged, what parked and why, and the next human action for each — one notification per parked issue, never one per failed step (SRE 1:1 alert/incident).
- The existing "were NOT started" message must actually reach the operator; it currently does not.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A group ending `handoff` or `aborted` parks and the remaining groups still run.
- [ ] A `quota-terminal` / `quota-window` classification halts the whole queue, because continuing would just burn every remaining issue against the same limit.
- [ ] A driver throw still halts (unchanged) — an unknown-shape failure is not safe to continue past.
- [ ] Parked entries carry enough to re-drive: issue, failing step, cap/cause, worktree path.
- [ ] End-of-queue summary lists merged / parked / halted with reasons.
- [ ] `PI_ENSEMBLE_QUEUE_HALT_ON_FAILURE=1` restores the old halt-on-first-failure behaviour.
- [ ] Offline test: inject a failure into group 2 of 5; assert groups 3-5 still run and the summary names group 2's reason.

## Doctrine

This reverses `docs/troubleshooting.md:705-717` and the halt-on-non-merged line in AGENTS.md §7. Both need updating with the rationale above.

## Out of scope

Running groups concurrently (#288 → #289). This issue changes only what happens *after* a group finishes; the pool stays sequential.
title: fix(work-driver): one failed group halts the entire queue — park it and continue instead
